sources.title: Interview note containing the three-sorted-array median question and the merge-until-middle solution note
Deterministic Java validation against a combined-sort oracle
Source-first isolated review for the median candidate

claims.text: The recovered source asks for the median of three sorted arrays with O(1) auxiliary space and records a merge-like strategy that stops around the middle; it does not preserve the even-length convention, element type, empty-array behavior, or a stronger time-complexity target.

With one pointer per sorted input, the smallest currently pointed-to value is the globally smallest unconsumed value; advancing only that source reproduces the prefix ranks of a three-way merge without materializing the merge.
The implementation stores only constant-sized scalar state and scans at most through the right-middle rank, giving O(1) auxiliary space and O(N) worst-case time for total input length N.

The exact Java implementation passes ten fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized sorted-array triples against a combined-sort oracle, preserves all inputs, and handles central-value integer extremes without addition overflow.

findings: The candidate is source-bounded and explicitly separates recovered facts from chosen API assumptions.
The correctness invariant and O(1) auxiliary-space argument are explicit and match the implementation.
The independent oracle covers randomized ordering combinations without reusing the candidate selection algorithm.
Integer-extreme fixed cases prove the average expression avoids int addition overflow.
No unsupported project, online-judge or hidden-constraint claims were introduced.
